quote: Hermes is MIT-licensed, model-agnostic and self-hosted, reachable through Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal or email, with persistent memory, self-written skills and a built-in scheduler. It is excellent, and it gave me the same magical feeling I had when I first set up OpenClaw. But it's definitely also a developer's tool, and most knowledge workers will find the setup intimidating.
author: Christian Pean
notes: Surgeon: Hermes excellent/OpenClaw-magic feel but developer-tool setup barrier.

quote: Running Opus 5.5 with a 1M window through a Claude subscription plugin in Hermes Agent burned the limit by lunch, because every turn re-read about 800K tokens of old chat. The fix: compress early and per model.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 27 Clauday: Hermes+Claude 1M re-read ~800K tokens/turn, burned limit by lunch.

quote: Raft is a Slack where humans and AI agents clock in together, and the team open-sourced the whole thing: server, web, CLI, the agent daemon and desktop app. Each agent has a name, role and memory stored locally; they claim tasks, hand off and review each other. Claude Code, Codex and Hermes can join a channel on your own subscription.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 27 Clauday: Raft open-source Slack-with-agents; Hermes can join.

quote: A solo founder says they are officially off the terminal and local development: a Claude-native workflow now hands back completed tasks backed by full end-to-end QA and verification. They tried the same idea early in the year with OpenClaw and Hermes and found it hacky; now it runs across code, design, marketing and support from anywhere.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 28 Clauday: early OpenClaw/Hermes hacky vs Claude-native now.

quote: Hermes takes the opposite posture openly. It is designed to work unattended between check-ins; that is the product, not an oversight. The question is not whether it will act without asking but where you have decided it must stop, and that decision has to be made before it touches real work rather than after.
author: Michael Brandt
notes: Yardwork: Hermes designed for unattended work; autonomy is the product.

quote: Bot Mode, on by default in the desktop app since August 31, turns Hermes profiles into named bots, each with its own model, memory, skills and routines… 250,000+ GitHub stars on September 30.
author: berkkalelioglu
notes: Sep 30 status snapshot.

quote: OpenClaw stronger for chat channels/multi-agent/skill library; Hermes stronger for learning/memory/safer defaults.
author: floriangray
notes: Gizmodo OpenClaw vs Hermes comparison.

quote: Writing a clear rule into a persona file is not the same as enforcing it; move enforcement to code before the model gets a turn.
author: rello1
notes: DEV: persona rules vs code enforcement lesson.

quote: Hermes Agent is a free, MIT licensed AI agent from Nous Research. It runs on your computer or a server, keeps memory between sessions, writes its own skills, and answers from a terminal or from Telegram, Slack and Discord.
author: mdchaitanya
notes: Munder Difflin Oct 3 explainer: Hermes is free MIT-licensed self-hosted agent.

quote: Pick Hermes Agent if you want memory and skills that grow, and a server to keep it on.
author: mdchaitanya
notes: Munder Difflin: Hermes for memory/skills growth with a server.

quote: An always-on agent with a shell is a colleague with root, one who never sleeps, reads everything you point it at, and will cheerfully print a secret to a log if nothing stops it. Security for that colleague is mostly about two questions: what can it reach, and what can it print.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura Oct 1: security framing for always-on shell agents.

quote: I run Hermes Agent in production on my own VPS. Every incident below actually happened to me. Every control below I checked in the source, not the marketing page.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura: production Hermes incidents verified against source.

quote: The agent should never hold a token it could print. The pattern that works is a proxy that holds the credential and a config that only ever points the agent at the proxy.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura: proxy pattern to keep credentials away from agents.

quote: Nous Research issued three sequential releases that archive reviewed project-management inputs as immutable sha256 objects. The approach prevents accidental edits during agent development cycles. Scripts manage the archive process to keep assets stable for repeated runs.
author: amyreed
notes: My AI Guide Oct 5: Hermes pinned inputs as sha256 for reproducibility.

quote: Two of the three most-starred software repositories on GitHub are agent harnesses, OpenClaw at 391,435 stars and Hermes Agent at 251,404, both read from the GitHub API on 5 October 2026.
author: ivantarin
notes: TechThoughtLeaders Oct 5: Hermes Agent 251k stars, #2 agent harness.

quote: Metis' AI agent platform ClawUp now lets anyone deploy their own AI agent in seconds from clawup.org. Users pick a runtime — OpenClaw (the default) or Hermes Agent — choose a model, and hit deploy, with no servers or setup; agents are provisioned in roughly 1–3 minutes.
author: metis
notes: ClawUp Oct 2: one-click Hermes deploy alongside OpenClaw.

quote: You want an assistant that learns your routines: Hermes. It turns repeated work into skills and changes models with one command. The install is bigger and the ecosystem is smaller.
author: alitariksahin
notes: Upstash Oct 9: Pick Hermes for learning routines + skills from repeated work.

quote: I run 5 Hermes agents and 4 Grok Bot agents. These days I reach for Grok Bot almost every time. The reason is simple: everything just works.
author: m0xt_
notes: Oct 12: Developer runs 5 Hermes agents but now reaches for Grok Bot more.

quote: IMO the era of Hermes & OpenClaw is now over. Over the last few months, ChatGPT has improved significantly and has nearly completely closed the gap on functionality of these tools.
author: maxekaplan
notes: Oct 12: Claims Hermes/OpenClaw era over as ChatGPT closes functionality gap.

quote: Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source autonomous agent, released under the MIT licence in February 2026. It keeps memory across sessions, writes reusable skills as it works, ships 70+ tools (web search, browser automation, vision, image generation, text-to-speech), connects through 20+ messaging gateways (Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Discord, Signal, email), works with any model provider from local to OpenRouter, and runs locally or in the cloud on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
author: thereisanaitool
notes: Oct 12 explainer: 70+ tools, 20+ messaging gateways, model-agnostic, MIT license.

quote: Pick Hermes if you want an agent runtime that lives on a server: seven execution backends including serverless sandboxes, a Mixture-of-Agents mode, and a model lab behind it.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura Oct 1: Pick Hermes for server runtime with 7 backends and Mixture-of-Agents.

quote: Hermes can execute in seven backends, three of them cloud sandboxes: Modal, Daytona and Vercel Sandbox. OpenClaw runs tools on the host unless you turn sandboxing on.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura: Hermes 7 backends vs OpenClaw host-default execution.

quote: My case is specific: a VPS, a cost-sensitive budget, and a fleet of work agents that an orchestrator wakes on its own schedule. I do not need a heartbeat, because the orchestrator is the heartbeat. I want commands to execute somewhere disposable. And my adapter, my agents' instruction bundles and my MCP pooler are all built around Hermes. For that case, Hermes is still the right call.
author: felipefontoura
notes: Fontoura: Stays with Hermes for VPS fleet with orchestrator-driven schedule.

quote: Hermes Agent — best for technical founders who want to own the harness, self-hosted, model-agnostic, and it distills completed work into reusable skills. Don't use it if you want turnkey, you are the operator, on-call for updates, containment, and your own model keys.
author: testedactually
notes: TestedActually Sep 24: Hermes for technical founders; self-hosted; distills skills.

quote: Full control and your own choice of model: Hermes or OpenClaw.
author: perkshelf
notes: PerkShelf Oct 15: Hermes or OpenClaw for full control and model choice.

quote: Honest question: if I'm already tweaking Hermes to be my own personal assistant, is there any benefit to using something like Muse or @bot?
author: brianmmdev
notes: X Oct 16: User already tweaking Hermes as personal assistant; asks if Muse adds value.

quote: What started as a FOMO experiment with the Hermes agent quickly turned into a full-blown packaging helper. When I started I had no clue of any use case but ended up using Hermes backed by solr4-pro from Upstage freely via Nous Research to complete a few pending things.
author: copyninja_
notes: X Oct 16: Hermes FOMO experiment became real packaging helper via Nous/Upstage free models.

quote: I've been wanting to get a sense of how the free models through Nous Portal fared if I used them for my various personal agents through Hermes. so I got my agent to build me an open benchmark called staffbench. it tests 9 different personal agent roles using those free models.
author: calvinnwq
notes: X Oct 16: Built staffbench to test 9 personal agent roles on Nous Portal free models via Hermes.

quote: Spent some time testing a fully local AI agent on my POCO X7 Pro using Termux, llama.cpp, and Hermes. Got real terminal execution working, but performance and command accuracy were another story.
author: datzholyg
notes: X Oct 16: Local Hermes agent on Android POCO X7 Pro via Termux/llama.cpp; terminal works but accuracy lacking.

quote: You might find Hermes Agent interesting to try. It's self-hosted grok bot. I really love it.
author: Loster
notes: X Oct 16: Describes Hermes as 'self-hosted grok bot'; loves it.

quote: Hermes, built by Nous Research, is the other self-hosted agent in my stack. Also MIT licensed, also on my own server. My instance, Nox, handles dev work: code, profiles, content pipelines. It has a learning loop that turns repeated tasks into reusable skills, which is genuinely useful for development workflows.
author: tunwin
notes: tun.lat Oct 15: Hermes handles dev work; learning loop turns repeated tasks into reusable skills.

quote: The honest story I owe you: recently my OpenClaw setup lost its Qwen models. I asked Muse, the agent helping me write this, to fix it. Three attempts, and each time it told me it was fixed. It was not. I took the same problem to Nox, which was already running a Qwen model at the time. Nox diagnosed the actual issue and fixed it in one go.
author: tunwin
notes: tun.lat Oct 15: Hermes fixed Qwen issue in one go that Muse failed 3x on.

quote: An open-source agent that lives in Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Signal or email. It runs scheduled jobs you describe in plain English, learns your repeat tasks, and works with 300+ cloud models or ones on your own computer.
author: novitckii
notes: novitckii Oct 2: Hermes lives in 6 messaging apps; 300+ cloud models or local; learns repeat tasks.

quote: By default it runs on your computer with no sandbox and can read any file you can. Model bills can spike. One user drained their whole balance in a 77-minute session. Connecting Gmail or Telegram is technical. Not for non-technical owners yet.
author: novitckii
notes: novitckii Oct 2: Hermes no sandbox by default; model bills can spike; Gmail/Telegram setup technical.

quote: Had a recurring issue where every Hermes update would delete my document tools like Word, PDF, etc.
author: u/hermesagent_user
notes: IADT Oct 19: Recurring issue where Hermes updates delete document tools (Word, PDF).

quote: I have a Hermes band manager bot. It does a weekly crawl of musician websites hunting and triaging a new member we're looking for. It keeps a list of options updated in Evernote (via MCP) and checks that list for anything I've updated.
author: u/hermesagent_user
notes: IADT Oct 19: Hermes band manager bot crawls musician sites weekly; updates Evernote via MCP.
